title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not Grothendieck's French manuscript on Galois theory of motives. The neighbouring pages are about CM tori and the groups M(q), G'. This page is a typed English translation, page '86', of a Russian-style text on algebraic surfaces or varieties. It cites a 'p. 208' of some source and its own numbered formulas (14), (21), (22), (23). It is almost certainly a stray or interleaved document in the folder.

The mathematics: V is a (projective) variety or surface, E' is a divisor, E'_ν is one of its components, and f_n is the rational map given by the linear system |nE'|.

1. From the restriction sequence 0 → O_V(-E'_ν)[nE'] → O_V[nE'] → O_{E'_ν}[nE'] → 0 and earlier estimates (14), (21), (22), one gets for n large dim H^1(V, O[nE']) = dim H^1(V, O(-E'_ν)[nE']), formula (23).
2. Choose m' ≥ n(E'_ν), where n(E'_ν) is presumably a threshold beyond which the restricted bundle on E'_ν has vanishing H^1 and is very ample, and large enough that (23) holds at n = m'.
3. Then the restriction H^0(V, O[m'E']) → H^0(E'_ν, O[m'E']|E'_ν) is surjective.
4. Hence f_{m'} restricted to E'_ν is the map given by the complete linear system on E'_ν, which is injective.
5. Next take q' with r = 2^{q'}m - m' > 0. To show f_{2^{q'}m} is injective on E'_ν, it suffices, for points P1 and P2, to find a section of O[2^{q'}mE'] vanishing at P1 but not at P2. The page breaks off here; presumably one multiplies a section of [m'E'] separating P1 and P2 by a section of [rE'] nonvanishing at both.

This is a standard step in proofs of ampleness or contractibility criteria (Zariski/Artin/Grauert/Nakai-type arguments), typical of the Shafarevich-seminar literature of the 1960s.
errors: The displayed sequence writes H^0(V, O_V[mE']); it should be [m'E'] to match the target.

Equality of the dimensions of the two H^1 groups alone does not give surjectivity of r^*. One also needs H^1(E'_ν, O[m'E']|E'_ν) = 0 (or injectivity of the next map), so that H^1(V, L(-E'_ν)) → H^1(V, L) is surjective and hence an isomorphism. Presumably this is encoded in the condition m' ≥ n(E'_ν).
The doubling 2^{q'}m suggests a Frobenius or symmetric-power trick from earlier pages, which are not visible here.

ideas.what: Surjectivity of restriction of sections to a component of a divisor via an H^1 dimension count, and the induced map on the component equal to its complete linear system.
ideas.modern_name: Restriction sequence / Serre vanishing argument for very ampleness and separation of points
ideas.usually_credited_to: Serre (FAC), Zariski, Kodaira; standard in 1960s surface theory (Shafarevich seminar)
ideas.where_published: Standard cohomological technique as in EGA III; not specific to this text

ideas.what: Separating points of E'_ν by sections of a higher multiple, using products of sections.
ideas.modern_name: Separation of points by sections of multiples of a semiample/nef divisor

It is unrelated to the surrounding CM-torus computations. This is an archival cataloguing point, not a mathematical discovery.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine step in a translated textbook or seminar argument about linear systems on a divisor, not by Grothendieck and unrelated to motives. The only oddity is its placement in the folder.
transcription_corrections: The displayed sequence reads H^0(V, O_V[mE']) in the typescript, but mathematically it should be [m'E'].
'H^0((E'_ν), O_{E'_ν}[m'E'])_{E'_ν})' is better read as H^0(E'_ν, O_{E'_ν}[m'E']|_{E'_ν}).
'transfered' is a typo in the original typescript.
